evidence.title: Audit Plus Worker Voice Program in Food Supply Chain

This initiative allows M&S to hear directly from workers, helping to identify cultural and engagement issues that could indicate or lead to human rights concerns.

evidence.title: Raw Material Risk Assessment and Sourcing Prioritization
evidence.summary: M&S conducted a comprehensive risk assessment of its top 50 raw materials to shape sourcing plans, prioritizing palm oil, soy, cocoa, tea, coffee, and timber due to environmental and social risks like deforestation and worker exploitation.
evidence.quote: This year, we conducted a comprehensive risk assessment of our top 50 raw materials, shaping our sourcing plan to prioritise those with the highest risks to drive positive change in our supply chains. evidence.title: New Multi-Temperature Depot Construction Near Bristol

evidence.quote: Capacity constraints mean that many stores do not receive their deliveries from the most efficient site. To support growth, work is underway on a new multi‑temperature depot in Bristol and to identify a site for a new national distribution centre.

evidence.title: Gist Acquisition Delivers Logistics Improvements and Profit

evidence.summary: M&S is implementing long-term supplier agreements across partner sites to protect quality while generating savings for reinvestment in quality and value, with plans to increase this approach in 2025/26.

evidence.title: Structural Cost Reductions Target of £500m Under Reshaping Strategy

evidence.title: Ongoing UK Store Estate Closure Programme

evidence.title: Automated distribution centre in Lichfield for Fashion supply chain
evidence.summary: M&S acquired and is integrating a 437,000 sq. ft. fully automated distribution centre in Lichfield to accelerate online capacity expansion for Fashion, Home & Beauty at lower capital cost, expected to start fulfilling orders in 2027.
evidence.quote: The recently announced investment in a 437,000 sq. ft. automated distribution centre in Lichfield will accelerate the expansion of online capacity earlier and at a lower capital cost than originally planned, while supporting network consolidation. It is expected that the new facility will start fulfilling customer orders in 2027, with a phased ramp-up thereafter.

initiatives.name: General Capital Expenditure Programme 2025/26
initiatives.summary: M&S plans capital expenditure of c.£600m-£650m for the current financial year, net of disposals, with £200m-£250m allocated to technology infrastructure, store maintenance, and logistics fleet, and £400m-£450m for growth and cost-out investment including new stores and supply chain capacity.

evidence.title: FY2025/26 Capital Expenditure Programme of £600m-£650m
evidence.summary: M&S plans capital expenditure of c.£600m-£650m for the current financial year, net of disposals, with £200m-£250m allocated to technology infrastructure, store maintenance, and logistics fleet, and £400m-£450m for growth and cost-out investment including new stores and supply chain capacity.
evidence.quote: A strong balance sheet enables additional investment and we are increasing capital expenditure net of disposals to c.£600m-£650m in 2025/26, of which £200m-£250m will be invested in further improving technology infrastructure, planned store maintenance and upgrades to the logistics fleet and network. Growth and cost-out investment is expected to be £400m-£450m, which includes increased new store openings and supply chain capacity.

initiatives.name: Employer National Insurance Contributions Adjustment
initiatives.summary: M&S's operating costs are set to significantly increase in 2025/26, driven by increases to employer National Insurance contributions following the UK Government's Autumn 2024 Budget, adding complexity to short and long-term financial planning.

evidence.title: Increased Employer National Insurance Contributions Impact
evidence.summary: M&S's operating costs are set to significantly increase in 2025/26, driven by increases to employer National Insurance contributions following the UK Government's Autumn 2024 Budget, adding complexity to short and long-term financial planning.
evidence.quote: While many hoped for a more stable UK economy in 2024/25, our operating costs are on track to significantly increase, principally driven by external factors: increases to employer NI contributions; FX headwinds; and slowing of store-based retail demand.

evidence.title: Plastic Reduction in Supply Chain and Transport
evidence.summary: The company reviewed supply chain operations, including plastic use from supplier to store, with committee members visiting a distribution centre to observe plastic reduction efforts firsthand. Potential future investments in alternative fuel sources for transport were also discussed.
evidence.quote: The Committee spent time reviewing our supply chain operations, including the opportunities and challenges to reaching our net zero targets, as well as use of plastic from supplier to store. To see the efforts to reduce plastic use first hand, Tamara Ingram and Cheryl Potter visited the Fashion, Home & Beauty distribution centre in Castle Donington.

initiatives.name: Carbon Tax Transition Risk Scenario
initiatives.summary: Scenario analysis identified that a potential carbon tax introduced in 2030 could have an operating profit impact of between £115m and £165m across Property, Fleet, Protein and Cotton categories if unmitigated, highlighting urgency of emissions reduction targets.

evidence.title: Carbon Tax Transition Risk Potential £115-165m Operating Profit Impact

evidence.quote: The scenario analysis identified that the transition risk associated with the introduction of a carbon tax in 2030 remains a material risk, with a potential operating profit impact across Property, Fleet, Protein and Cotton of between £115m and £165m assuming no mitigation.
